newsitem.title: USA: US April jobs revision reflects sampling update.
newsitem.headline: US April jobs revision reflects sampling update.

text.p: The big upward revision in the April payroll number in the latest monthly employment report reflects in part an annual update of the Labor Department's procedures for sampling job growth at different-sized companies, a department official said Friday.
April payroll growth, as reported in the May employment report, was revised upward to 323,000 from 142,000.

The revised number reflects an updating of the size of each company that is surveyed for the payroll report -- a factor that is believed to have been a "major contributor" to the overall April revision, according to the official.
Here is how the updating works.
The department tracks payroll growth at companies of varying sizes, based on the number of persons employed.
For example, those with fewer than 50 employees are assigned to one class of firms, while those with more than 50 are assigned to a category of larger companies.

Each year at this time the department will reassign the companies among the different categories depending on whether they have gained or lost enough employees so that they would join a different class of firms based on their size.
The updating affects the revised April number each year that is contained in the May data reported in June.
The department official said it is typical that the revised April number, as a result, contains a hefty revision.
But this year's revision was larger than usual and department officials do not have an immediate explanation for the increase.

Other factors also are at work. The department official said that revised seasonal-adjustment factors account for about 50,000 of the 181,000 revision. The annual benchmark revisions also play a role.
And like every month, the department has more data on which to make a better estimate of payrolls for a previously reported month.
